name: Max Kreminski
title: Six Fingers on the Author’s Hand
abstract: Creative processes across a wide variety of domains increasingly incorporate AI-based tools, but what are the implications for human authorship? In this three-act talk, I first recap my work on AI-driven homogenization of creative output, the "dearth of the author", and recurring interaction dynamics in human-AI co-creativity. Next, I present several related AI-based authoring tools that aim to extend and mutate the practice of authorship in a particular domain (interactive storytelling), enabling human authors to reassert some control over radically open-ended forms of expressive media. Finally, I discuss how we (as creative practitioners) increasingly find ourselves struggling to make sense of and navigate a rapidly expanding frontier – with implications for the design of AI tools meant to support professional designers, artistic curators, scientific researchers, and more.
bio: Max Kreminski is an assistant professor of Design Tech at Cornell Tech. As a human-computer interaction and AI researcher with a particular focus on creativity support tools, Max has worked to create new interfaces, interaction techniques, and models that can scaffold creative processes in a wide variety of domains, as well as to introduce new, domain-general methods for evaluating CSTs. Max's research has been featured in outlets such as The New Yorker, New Scientist, and The Verge; published and exhibited at top HCI and AI conferences, including CHI, UIST, NeurIPS, and EMNLP; and honored with a variety of awards, including the Best Paper award at the ACM Conference on Creativity & Cognition.
